mainEntity.name: How can UPS battery ride-through be estimated from nameplate capacity?

acceptedAnswer.text: An illustrative idealized energy-balance estimate of UPS ride-through time (t) in seconds is: t = (E_nom * eta_dis * eta_dist / P_crit) * 3600, where E_nom is nominal battery capacity in kWh, eta_dis is battery discharge efficiency (typically 0.90 to 0.94), eta_dist is distribution path efficiency (typically 0.95), and P_crit is critical IT load in kW. For a 100 kWh battery pack supporting a 1000 kW (1 MW) critical IT load at 0.90 discharge and 0.95 distribution efficiency, the idealized arithmetic result is: 100 * 0.90 * 0.95 / 1000 * 3600 = 307.8 seconds (5.13 minutes). Actual usable runtime depends on discharge limits, conversion losses, load characteristics, temperature, and equipment ratings; this is not a Tier IV compliance assessment.

mainEntity.name: What causes DC-link voltage collapse during generator transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: DC-link voltage collapse occurs when the rate of capacitor discharge exceeds rectifier input recharge during the open-transition transfer interval (t_transfer). The differential equation governing DC-link voltage is: C_dc * (dV_dc / dt) = I_rectifier - I_inverter. If the emergency diesel generator (EDG) startup delay plus Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) slew time exceeds the critical capacitor hold-up duration without instantaneous BESS discharge support, V_dc drops below the under-voltage lockout threshold (typically 0.85 * V_nominal), triggering an emergency inverter shutdown.
